detail.longDescription: I am working on a simple GUI interface using Tkinter that takes the name and the displays a welcome message when you click a button, but I need to split the GUI code to a file and the function of say_hello to another file, I do not want the code in one file. main.py : from tkinter import Tk , Label , Button , Entry , END from welcome import say_hello window = Tk() window.title("Welcome User") window.geometry("400x300") askName = Label(window , text="Enter Your own name : ") askName.pack(pady=20) nameEntry = Entry(window , width=24) nameEntry.pack(pady=10) btn = Button(window , text="Say Hello" , command=say_hello) btn.pack(pady=10) welcomeUser = Label(window , text="Waiting Your Name") welcomeUser.pack(pady=20) window.mainloop() welcome.py : from main import nameEntry , welcomeUser def say_hello(): userName = nameEntry.get() welcomeUser.config(text=f"Welcome in our Program {userName}") userName.delete(0,END) The error message is: Traceback (most recent call last): File "c:\Users\hp\Desktop\Matplotlib_tutorial\Python_GUI\main.py", line 2, in <module> from welcome import say_hello File "c:\Users\hp\Desktop\Matplotlib_tutorial\Python_GUI\welcome.py", line 2, in <module> from main import nameEntry , welcomeUser File "c:\Users\hp\Desktop\Matplotlib_tutorial\Python_GUI\main.py", line 2, in <module> from welcome import say_hello ImportError: cannot import name 'say_hello' from 'welcome' (consider renaming 'c:\\Users\\hp\\Desktop\\Matplotlib_tutorial\\Python_GUI\\welcome.py' if it has the same name as a library you intended to import)
